rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm guarded against: a body sentence doing the forcing-function's job means speed-runners who skip prose still miss nothing load-bearing, but also means the mandate isn't actually enforced by the fence. Single fenced prompt in file: `{{prompt:what-packaging-is-1}}` (grep -n → line 231). Its registry body (curriculum/prompts/what-packaging-is-1.md) carries the full instruction ('Propose five hooks... name the event... skip suggestions any team could want. No preamble. List them.'). The body line immediately above it (line 229: 'Ask Claude to propose five hooks tied to this repo, beyond formatting and linting') is a one-clause lead-in naming what's coming, not a restatement of the prompt's constraints (no event-naming requirement, no anti-generic instruction, no output-format instruction repeated in body). Stripping the body line and reading the prompt alone still delivers the full forcing function — diagnostic in the rule is satisfied.
